proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched class-wide n^-2/5 root-MSE bound using local redistribution weights and an observed-law Gaussian lower-bound pair; it also established the strict-overlap root-n elbow. D0.5 judged the result subfield because the fixed-design modulus is open and the package does not clear the field significance threshold. The panel stopped before repairing unused assumptions and missing citation-relevance prose; there is no Lean formalization.
tldr: Marginal quantile treatment effects remain point identified under one-sided weak overlap, but ordinary inverse weighting can have infinite variance. The exact-integral estimator softly clips the known propensity and redistributes the removed target mass only to nearby covariates with positive, design-computable weights. Lipschitz conditional CDFs give transport bias of order \(t\), the square-root overlap tail gives variance of order \(n^{-1}t^{-1/2}\), and \(t=n^{-2/5}\) yields root-MSE \(n^{-2/5}\) without a logarithmic loss. A fully specified Gaussian causal pair at \(e(x)=x^2/2\) gives two induced observed-data laws with matching QTE separation and exact divergence in both directions. An optional certified interval-evaluation interface yields an executable corollary at the same rate without narrowing the abstract propensity class.
gap: Published weak-overlap QTE theory gives truncated-IPW limit laws, and published weak-overlap minimax theory gives linear-functional or regression frontiers. No inspected theorem evaluates the minimax risk of a full-population marginal QTE over the stated one-dimensional Lipschitz conditional-CDF class.
fill: Positive local mass redistribution produces an explicit monotone weighted CDF, a no-log maximal inequality and clipped inversion yield the upper rate, and a legal Gaussian causal observation-law pair yields the matching lower rate.
